evidence.sourceText: The chaste Diana was not only a famous huntress, but she was goddess of the moon as well.
Diana was not susceptible to love; but when she saw Endymion sleeping, she marveled at his beauty, and felt a strange longing to be near him.

As soon as Apollo had driven his tired, foam-flecked horses within the western gates, and twilight had begun to creep over the hills, Diana mounted her silver car drawn by milk-white steeds, and started on her nightly journey.

narrative.synopsis: Diana sees Endymion sleeping by moonlight and repeatedly visits him. Wanting him to remain beautiful and young, she takes him to Mount Latmus and causes eternal sleep to fall on him.
narrative.openingSituation: Diana makes her nightly moon journey after Apollo's sun course ends.
narrative.centralConflict: Diana longs to remain near the sleeping Endymion without waking him.
narrative.resolution: Diana takes Endymion to a cave on Mount Latmus.
narrative.outcome: Endymion remains in eternal sleep, and Diana visits him every night.
